chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abi Wallad al-Hannat, who said:
I asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who was killed, and he had a father, a mother, and a son.
Then the son said: I want to kill the killer of my father. And the father said: I pardon. And the mother said: I take the blood money.

He عليه السلام said: Then the son should give the mother of the slain one one-sixth of the blood money, and he should give the heirs of the killer one-sixth of the blood money, representing the right of the father who pardoned him, and then he may kill him.

key_terms.الدِّيَةَ: the blood money owed in compensation for killing
key_terms.السُّدُسَ: one-sixth, the specified share mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.الِابْنُ: the son, who seeks qisas in this case
key_terms.الْأَبُ: the father, who waives his right
key_terms.الْأُمُّ: the mother, who chooses blood money
key_terms.عَفَا: pardoned or waived the right of retaliation
key_terms.وَرَثَةَ: the heirs, here the heirs of the killer

ai.seo_question: How is qisas applied when the heirs of a murder victim disagree between retaliation, pardon, and blood money?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding conflicting claims of the heirs of a murder victim in the matter of qisas and diyah. It establishes that when one heir seeks retaliation, another waives his right, and another seeks compensation, the right of each is financially accounted for before qisas is carried out.
